mcqs.q: An articulator is:
opts: A mechanical device that represents the TMJ and jaw members and simulates mandibular movement
A negative imprint of the dental arch
mcqs.explain: The articulator mechanically represents the TMJ/jaws and simulates mandibular motion.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of an articulator?
opts: To act as a patient in the patient's absence for diagnosis and appliance fabrication
To take the patient's blood pressure
mcqs.explain: Uses: substitute for the patient, aid diagnosis/planning, study occlusion, fabricate/adjust restorations.

mcqs.q: Which component provides the positive anterior vertical stop of an articulator?
mcqs.explain: The incisal pin rests on the incisal table, giving the anterior vertical stop.

mcqs.q: A simple-hinge (non-adjustable) articulator:
opts: Simulates only opening and closing and is not related to an anatomical axis
mcqs.explain: The simple hinge allows only open/close and ignores the true hinge axis, losing accuracy.

mcqs.q: A key DISADVANTAGE of the simple-hinge articulator is that:
opts: The tooth-to-axis distance is shorter than in the skull, causing loss of accuracy
It is far too expensive for routine use
It reproduces too much intermediate movement
It cannot be opened or closed
mcqs.explain: The shortened tooth–axis distance introduces non-working interferences and loss of accuracy.

mcqs.q: Semi-adjustable articulators reproduce the:
opts: Direction and end point of movement, but not the intermediate tract
mcqs.explain: They simulate the condylar path as a straight line (direction + end point), not the curved intermediate tract.

mcqs.q: In an ARCON articulator, the condylar elements (spheres) are located on the:
opts: Lower member, with the mechanical fossa on the upper member
Upper member, with the fossa on the lower member
mcqs.explain: Arcon = Articulator + Condyle: condylar spheres on the lower member and fossae on the upper (like the skull); Non-Arcon is the reverse.

mcqs.q: The Hanau semi-adjustable articulator accepts which single eccentric record?
mcqs.explain: Hanau accepts one eccentric (protrusive) record; the condylar inclination is set until the teeth fit it.

mcqs.q: Fully-adjustable articulators are chiefly used for:
opts: Full-mouth rehabilitation, adjusted to a pantograph tracing
mcqs.explain: They reproduce 3-D border movements from a pantograph and are used for full-mouth rehabilitation.

mcqs.q: Hanau's formula for the lateral condylar angle is:
mcqs.explain: The lateral condylar guidance is estimated from the horizontal angle: L = [H/8] + 12.

mcqs.q: A face-bow is used to:
opts: Record the maxillary teeth relation to the hinge axis and mount the maxillary cast
Measure the vertical dimension of occlusion
mcqs.explain: The face-bow transfers the maxilla-to-hinge-axis relationship so the maxillary cast is mounted correctly.

mcqs.q: The arbitrary face-bow consists of a U-shaped bow, a bite fork, and:
opts: Two posterior and one anterior reference points
One posterior and three anterior reference points
mcqs.explain: It uses two posterior reference points plus one anterior reference point to orient the maxillary cast.

mcqs.q: Which is used as an ANTERIOR reference point for a face-bow?
opts: Nasion (Whip Mix) / infra-orbital notch (Hanau) / 43 mm above the incisal edge (Denar)
mcqs.explain: Anterior reference points: nasion, infra-orbital notch, or 43 mm above the maxillary incisal edge, depending on the system.

mcqs.q: The kinematic (hinge-axis) face-bow differs from the arbitrary one because it:
opts: Accurately locates the true hinge axis
Uses an average, assumed hinge axis
Does not require any reference points
mcqs.explain: The kinematic face-bow records the true hinge axis via styli that trace pure rotation, then transfers it. Recorded from mandibular movement.

mcqs.q: Centric relation (CR) is a maxillomandibular relationship that is:
opts: Independent of tooth contact, with condyles anterosuperior against the eminences
Defined only by maximum tooth intercuspation
mcqs.explain: CR places the condyle–disk complexes anterosuperiorly against the eminences and is independent of tooth contact (terminal hinge).

mcqs.q: Which material is used for interocclusal records?
opts: Wax, plaster of Paris, ZOE paste, or polyvinyl (PVS) registration material
mcqs.explain: Interocclusal records use wax, plaster of Paris, ZOE paste, or PVS registration material.

mcqs.q: Which is a stated use of an articulator?
opts: To act as a patient in the absence of the patient
To record the centric relation intra-orally
To measure the vertical dimension clinically
mcqs.explain: It also aids diagnosis and treatment planning, the study of occlusion and mandibular movements, the fabrication of appliances, and the correction of completed restorations.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a component of an articulator?
opts: A bite fork and locking device
Styli attached to the mandibular teeth
mcqs.explain: The upper and lower members, the incisal pin and the incisal table are the others; the bow, bite fork and styli belong to face-bows.

mcqs.q: Among the requirements of an articulator is that it should:
opts: Accept a face-bow transfer, with rigid and moving parts that resist wear
Reproduce the intermediate tract of condylar movement
Have a fully adjustable intercondylar distance
mcqs.explain: It must also maintain the correct centric position, include a positive anterior vertical stop, open and close in a hinge movement, allow protrusive and lateral motion, and give adequate distance and unobstructed vision.

mcqs.q: The average-value (mean-value) articulator differs from the simple hinge in that it:
opts: Permits vertical as well as horizontal motion and is anatomically related to the TMJs
Has a fully adjustable intercondylar distance
mcqs.explain: It is based on mean mandibular movements.

mcqs.q: A semi-adjustable articulator reproduces:
opts: The direction and end point of mandibular movement, but not the intermediate tract
The complete border movements including intermediate pathways
mcqs.explain: The condylar path is simulated as a straight line rather than a curve.

mcqs.q: Which are examples of semi-adjustable articulators?
opts: Hanau, Whip-Mix and Denar Mark II
mcqs.explain: They offer a close, though not precise, approximation of the axis-to-teeth distance.

mcqs.q: A stated disadvantage of the semi-adjustable articulator is that:
opts: Intercondylar distance is not fully adjustable, so some intraoral adjustment may be needed
It is unable to accept a face-bow transfer
It permits a hinge movement and nothing else
It is unable to accept eccentric interocclusal records
mcqs.explain: Only the fully-adjustable instrument has an adjustable intercondylar distance.

mcqs.q: The Hanau semi-adjustable articulator accepts which eccentric record?
opts: Neither — it accepts only centric records
mcqs.explain: The patient holds the jaw in a protruded relationship while the record is taken; the condylar inclination is then adjusted until the teeth fit the record accurately.

mcqs.q: Fully-adjustable articulators are adjusted using:
mcqs.explain: They accept 3-D dynamic registrations and reproduce the border movements of the mandible, and are used for full-mouth rehabilitations.

mcqs.q: A stated disadvantage of the fully-adjustable articulator is that it is:
opts: Expensive, demanding of a high degree of skill, and time-consuming
mcqs.explain: Its complex condylar mechanism replicates the recorded three-dimensional motion.

mcqs.q: On a mean-value articulator, the horizontal condylar angle is:
mcqs.explain: Its lateral condylar angle and incisal guidance angle are likewise fixed.

mcqs.q: Which articulator type has an ADJUSTABLE intercondylar distance?
mcqs.explain: It is fixed on the mean-value and semi-adjustable instruments.

mcqs.q: Which face-bow is required for a FULLY-adjustable articulator?
mcqs.explain: The semi-adjustable articulator requires an arbitrary face-bow; the simple hinge and mean-value instruments require none.

mcqs.q: The kinematic hinge-axis face-bow locates the true hinge axis in two steps, the first being:
opts: Hinge-axis recording — styli on the mandibular teeth are adjusted until they show pure rotation
Kinematic face-bow transfer to the articulator
mcqs.explain: Step 2 is the kinematic face-bow transfer, which transfers the relation between the maxilla and the TMJ.

mcqs.q: The anterior and two posterior reference points of a face-bow together establish the:
mcqs.explain: This lets the maxillary cast be transferred so that its occlusal-plane relationship in the articulator matches the patient's skull.

mcqs.q: Which anterior reference point is used with the Hanau system?
opts: 43 mm above the incisal edge of the maxillary teeth
mcqs.explain: Nasion is used by Whip-Mix and the 43 mm point by Denar Mark II.

mcqs.q: Which is a material used for interocclusal records?
mcqs.explain: Wax, plaster of Paris and zinc oxide–eugenol paste are the other three.

saqs.q: Define an articulator and list four of its uses.
saqs.a: An ARTICULATOR is a mechanical device representing the TMJ and jaw members and simulating mandibular movement. Uses: acts as the patient in the patient's absence · aids diagnosis and treatment planning · studies occlusion and mandibular movements · helps fabricate appliances · corrects and modifies completed restorations.

ans.text: A mechanical device representing the TMJ and jaw members and simulating mandibular movement.

list: Acts as the patient, in the patient's absence

saqs.q: Classify articulators and give one feature of each class.
saqs.a: NON-ADJUSTABLE — simple hinge (open/close only, no true axis) and mean-value (vertical + horizontal, based on average movements). SEMI-ADJUSTABLE (arcon/non-arcon) — adjustable condylar and incisal guides, accepting centric and eccentric records and a face-bow. FULLY-ADJUSTABLE — adjustable intercondylar distance, reproducing 3-D border movements from a pantograph; for full-mouth rehabilitation.

adjustable condylar and incisal guides; accepts centric and eccentric records and a face-bow
adjustable intercondylar distance; reproduces 3-D border movements from a pantograph — used for full-mouth rehabilitation

saqs.a: ARCON (Articulator + Condyle) — condylar elements on the LOWER member, mechanical fossae on the UPPER, mimicking the skull. NON-ARCON — condylar elements on the UPPER member, condylar path on the LOWER.

saqs.q: What is a face-bow used for, and what are its two types?
saqs.a: A FACE-BOW records the relationship of the maxillary teeth to the rotational (hinge) centre of the jaw and transfers it to the articulator, so the maxillary cast is mounted as it sits in the skull. Types: ARBITRARY (average hinge-axis) and KINEMATIC (true hinge-axis).

ans.text: Records the relationship of the maxillary teeth to the rotational (hinge) centre of the jaw and transfers it to the articulator, so the maxillary cast is mounted in the same relationship as in the skull.

saqs.q: Define centric relation and name two other interocclusal records.
saqs.a: CENTRIC RELATION — the maxillomandibular relationship with the condyle-disk complexes in the anterosuperior position against the articular eminences (thinnest avascular disk portion), INDEPENDENT of tooth contact; opening and closing about it are purely rotational (terminal hinge). Other records: maximum intercuspation, and lateral and protrusive interocclusal records.

ans.text: CENTRIC RELATION — the maxillomandibular relationship in which the condyle-disk complexes are in the anterosuperior position against the articular eminences, with the thinnest avascular portion of the disk, independent of tooth contact. Opening and closing about it are purely rotational — the terminal hinge.

saqs.q: List the components and the requirements of an articulator.
saqs.a: COMPONENTS — upper and lower members; condyle posts and condylar guides; incisal pin and incisal table. REQUIREMENTS — maintain the correct centric position; a positive anterior vertical stop (the incisal pin); hinge opening and closing plus protrusive and lateral motion; accept a face-bow transfer; rigid and moving parts that resist wear; adequate distance between members without obscuring vision.

list: Include a positive anterior vertical stop — the incisal pin
Open and close in a hinge movement, and allow protrusive and lateral motion
Rigid and moving parts that resist wear
Allow adequate distance between members without obscuring vision

saqs.q: Compare the four classes of articulator with respect to condylar angles, intercondylar distance and face-bow requirement.
saqs.a: SIMPLE HINGE — no condylar or incisal angles, no pin, no face-bow. MEAN-VALUE — horizontal 30° fixed, lateral and incisal fixed, pin available, intercondylar fixed, no face-bow (Bonwill triangle). SEMI-ADJUSTABLE — horizontal adjustable by protrusive record, lateral by Hanau L = H/8 + 12, incisal adjustable, pin available, intercondylar FIXED, ARBITRARY face-bow. FULLY ADJUSTABLE — horizontal and lateral adjustable, incisal adjustable, pin available, intercondylar ADJUSTABLE, KINEMATIC face-bow.
